concerns.text: Power analysis (bullet 1) assumes a medium effect size (f = 0.25) without empirical justification. The claimed ≥80 % power for the Friedman test may be optimistic; a sensitivity analysis or pilot data should be provided to support the effect‑size choice.

Intent‑entity extraction (bullet 4) relies on a zero‑shot classifier calibrated on a 200‑sample gold set, yet fidelity scoring (bullet 6) is performed on all ≥500 samples. The majority of intent scores therefore lack human‑annotated ground truth, threatening construct validity of the ‘intent precision/recall’ metrics.

Stratified sampling controls for commit‑message length, diff size, and documentation complexity, but does not stratify by repository, programming language, or project size. These unmodeled factors could confound observed differences between models, violating the Architectural Fidelity Isolation principle.

Multiple‑comparison correction applies Holm‑Bonferroni across three metrics and a Nemenyi post‑hoc test, yet the plan also conducts separate Friedman/ANOVA tests per metric. The correction strategy is unclear and may not adequately control the family‑wise error rate across all tests.
